comparison: Both strongly support claims about EPCR as a reliable HSC marker (C43-C51, C58, C126, C128). OpenEval provides detailed analysis of transplantation data showing EPCRhigh cells produce long-term reconstitution. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the authors 'functionally establishing EPCR (CD201) as a reliable and stable HSC marker' with convincing functional data.

Perfect agreement on FL-cHSC expansion claims (C101-C103, C105, C141-C142). Both support that fetal liver HSCs expand less than adult counterparts in PVA cultures. OpenEval notes reduced reconstitution suggesting the culture system may not support all HSC types equally. Peer reviewers find this a useful and valuable finding without challenge.

Perfect agreement on CD45 mismatch barrier claims (C110-C111, C171). Both support that unconditioned CD45-mismatched recipients show no long-term reconstitution, contrasting with successful F1 host engraftment. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this as an important technical consideration addressed in experimental design.

Strong agreement on HSC heterogeneity and clonal barcoding claims (C3, C42, C93-C96, C106, C135-C136). OpenEval emphasizes pre-culture barcoding showing extensive clone size variation and correlation with reconstitution. Peer reviewers praise the 'elegant' use of 'state-of-the-art barcoding strategies' and note this is 'the first to my knowledge to use barcoding to quantify HSC repopulation capacity at the clonal level after PVA culture.'

Both support claims about cHSC frequency decrease with substantial fold-expansion (C1, C64, C75, C131, C133). OpenEval analyzes phenotypic data showing decreasing frequency but increasing absolute numbers. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'only very few cells within these cultures have long-term repopulation capacity' and 'robust expansion of cHSCs' as key findings with convincing data.

Both support unconditioned transplantation claims (C6, C112, C122, C172), though OpenEval focuses on engraftment data while peer review also emphasizes quiescence (C7, C123, C173-C174 covered in R12). OpenEval highlights CD45-matched system overcoming immunological barriers. Peer reviewers explicitly note 'expanded HSCs can be engrafted in unconditioned host' as a novel key finding.

Both support quiescence and return to dormancy claims (C7, C117-C121, C123, C173-C174). OpenEval analyzes CellTrace Violet data showing few divisions and correlation between quiescence and EPCR expression. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'expanded HSCs can be engrafted in unconditioned host and return to quiescence' as a key finding.

Both address single-cell multiome characterization (C65-C68, C77), but with different emphasis. OpenEval supports claims about cluster identification, HSC signature localization, and trajectory analysis. Peer reviewers acknowledge this as 'the first report characterising output of PVA cultures by multiome' but express disappointment, noting 'The analysis of the multiome experiment is limited' and authors 'miss out on the opportunity to take a deeper dive into the molecular characteristics.'

Both support radioprotection and progenitor activity claims (C52-C57, C59 in OpenEval; C4-C5, C54-C57, C59, C81-C84 in peer review). OpenEval focuses on survival correlation with EPCR expression. Peer reviewers explicitly note 'many others however have progenitor properties which can rescue mice from lethal myeloablation' as a key finding, acknowledging the distinction between transient and long-term reconstituting populations.

Overlapping support for EPCRhighCD48-/low long-term reconstitution (C2, C79-C85, C132 in OpenEval; C81-C84 in peer review). OpenEval provides detailed analysis of transplantation data showing robust multilineage reconstitution from EPCRhighCD48-/low cells. Peer reviewers acknowledge the functional characterization of different populations as part of key findings.

Both support competitive transplantation and HSC expansion quantification claims (C86-C92, C104 in OpenEval; C86, C92, C104, C155 in peer review). OpenEval analyzes variable reconstitution from individual cultures versus consistent pooled activity. Peer reviewers describe functional analyses as 'convincing' and acknowledge 'robust increases in HSC activity following culture.'

Both support post-culture barcoding claims showing more even clone distribution (C97-C100, C137-C138 in OpenEval; C137-C138 in peer review). OpenEval emphasizes significantly smaller median clone sizes and reduced dominant clones. Peer reviewers acknowledge barcoding 'unequivocally' demonstrates HSC self-renewal as part of their broader support for the barcoding approach.

Both support interpretation of true self-renewal versus alternative mechanisms (C139-C140 in OpenEval; C139-C140, C144-C145, C157 in peer review). OpenEval uses barcoding data to argue for true self-renewal rather than enhanced homing. Peer reviewers explicitly state the study 'independently validates that the proposed culturing system works and provide new insights into the mechanisms whereby HSC expansion takes place.'

Both support claims about EPCRhighCD48+ cells showing transient activity (C4, C81, C159, C162 in OpenEval; C4, C81-C84 in peer review). OpenEval emphasizes high initial reconstitution that drops over time, clarifying these are non-self-renewing progenitors. Peer reviewers acknowledge the distinction between transient and long-term populations as important characterization.

Both support radioprotection claims (C5, C54, C59, C147 in OpenEval; C5, C54-C57, C59 in peer review). OpenEval focuses on correlation between EPCR expression and survival with efficient rescue from lethal irradiation. Peer reviewers acknowledge progenitor properties that 'can rescue mice from lethal myeloablation' as a key finding.

Minimal overlap on Fgd5+ cell heterogeneity (C72-C74, C78 in OpenEval; C78 in peer review). OpenEval supports claims about heterogeneous CD48 expression and single-cell multiome limitations. Peer reviewers' evaluation of multiome data is more critical overall, noting limited analysis, though they don't specifically address Fgd5+ heterogeneity.

OpenEval supports claims about EPCR+ cells having more even HSC signature distribution with cell cycle as primary variation source (C69-C71). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific molecular characterization claims.

OpenEval supports claim C49 about CD41 staining not affecting engraftment, contradicting Gekas and Graf 2013. Peer reviewers don't specifically address this methodological point but broadly support the EPCR marker validation that includes this data.

OpenEval supports claims about correlation between myeloid and cHSC RUs and rationale based on lineage turnover rates (C89, C158, C164-C165). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific quantification methodology claims.

OpenEval supports claims about higher initial cHSC chimerism from expanded cells that equalizes over time (C115-C116). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific kinetic observations.

Both support interpretation of variable individual culture reconstitution versus consistent pooled activity (C152, C155-C157 in OpenEval; C155 in peer review). OpenEval emphasizes intrinsic regulation interpretation. Peer reviewers accept the quantification of expansion as part of valuable PVA system characterization.

Both acknowledge limitations in resolving CD48 heterogeneity (C134 in OpenEval; C134 in peer review context). OpenEval frames this as an acknowledged technical limitation requiring functional assays. Peer reviewers note the multiome analysis is limited and missed opportunities for deeper molecular characterization.
OpenEval supports standard background knowledge claims (C8-C14) establishing study rationale. No corresponding peer review evaluation found as these are cited background rather than novel findings.
OpenEval supports claims accurately citing Wilkinson et al. 2019 (C15-C20, C60-C61) as foundation for current study. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these citation claims.

OpenEval supports claims about well-documented CRA limitations (C26-C36) establishing rationale for improved quantification methods. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological background claims.

OpenEval supports claims about conditioning requirements (C37-C41) providing rationale for unconditioned transplantation experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims, though peer reviewers support the unconditioned transplantation results.
OpenEval supports established knowledge claims (C21-C23) about assessing both HSC and progenitor activity. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval supports standard methodology claims (C24-C25) establishing experimental context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological background claims.

Both support synthesis of recent literature on native hematopoiesis (C143-C146 in OpenEval; C144-C145 in peer review). OpenEval connects cited literature to current findings. Peer reviewers acknowledge the study provides 'new insights into the mechanisms whereby HSC expansion takes place.'

Both address application of multiome data to study differentiation (C148-C149 in OpenEval; C149 in peer review). OpenEval supports this as valid application showing trajectories and molecular features. Peer reviewers acknowledge potential value but express disappointment that deeper analysis wasn't included.

OpenEval supports reasonable inference about limitations for large-scale screens (C150-C151) based on limited functional HSC expansion versus total cell expansion. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific application limitation claims.

OpenEval supports claims about field state and enabling role of barcoding (C153-C154). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers praise the barcoding approach as novel and elegant.
OpenEval supports immunological interpretation of lymphoid reconstitution data (C160-C161, C163). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific mechanistic interpretation claims.
OpenEval rates claim C166 as UNCERTAIN due to 'data not shown' despite consistency with cited work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific observation.

OpenEval supports established knowledge claims (C167-C170) providing rationale for unconditioned transplantation experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims, though peer reviewers support the experimental results.
OpenEval supports reasonable inference about clinical implications (C175). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this forward-looking claim.
OpenEval supports concluding statements about general knowledge and future applications (C176-C177). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these forward-looking claims.
OpenEval supports accurate citation of Gekas and Graf 2013 (C44), though current study contradicts antibody interference aspect. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this citation claim.

OpenEval supports claims about high reconstitution in irradiated hosts (C107-C109) establishing cultured cell capacity. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific control experiment claims.

OpenEval supports claims about established knowledge and inference regarding cell cycle state contrast (C113-C114). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific mechanistic claims.

Both support synthesis of prior work with current EPCR enrichment findings (C124-C130 in OpenEval; C126, C128 in peer review). OpenEval provides comprehensive synthesis including field adoption assessment. Peer reviewers focus on functional validation of EPCR as reliable HSC marker.
